items.title: The End of the Gupta Empire
items.explanation: By the end of the 6th century, the powerful Gupta Empire had lost its dominance in northern India. This marked a significant shift where regional powers began to emerge instead of a single central empire.

items.title: The Rise of Harṣhavardhana
items.explanation: Harṣhavardhana, known as the 'Great King of Kings', ascended to the throne in 606 CE at Kannauj. He belonged to the Puṣhyabhūti dynasty and expanded his influence over large parts of northern and eastern India.

items.title: Regional Powers and Cultural Diversity
items.explanation: The period saw a land buzzing with new ideas, art, and culture. While empires were less dominant, strong kingdoms like the Pallavas in the south and the Pālas in Bengal continued to support great universities and carve magnificent temples.
